content: Welcome to Tweetbook. This platform was created with the goal of preserving intriguing, peer-reviewed case reports in the field of interventional cardiology. Its purpose is to foster meaningful discussions about these cases by leveraging the active engagement of the Twitter cardiology community. We are specifically interested in case reports that pertain to interventional cardiology. These topics include, but are not limited to, the following areas: Hemodynamic studies and abnormalities. Diseases affecting the pericardium. Intravascular imaging and physiologic assessments. Pathologies involving the left main coronary artery. Management of bifurcation lesions. Techniques and outcomes of coronary artery stenting. Coronary atherectomy procedures. Coronary thrombectomy techniques. Treatment of chronic total occlusions. Interventions involving coronary bypass grafts. Cases of spontaneous coronary artery dissection. Disorders of the coronary microvasculature. Coronary artery anomalies and aneurysms. Percutaneous valve therapies. Management of congenital heart disease. Left atrial appendage occlusion procedures. Cardiogenic shock and the use of mechanical support devices. Peripheral vascular disease interventions. Complications arising from interventional procedures. Pharmacological approaches in interventional cardiology. Acute coronary syndromes. Noninvasive cardiovascular imaging techniques. Miscellaneous topics relevant to interventional cardiology. To submit a case report, please email it to the editorial office at tweetbook@wikidoc.org for peer review. Case reports should include imaging studies or pictures that highlight significant classic or novel findings, provide insights into fundamental mechanisms, emphasize abnormalities, or introduce potential new techniques or roles for noninvasive interventions. Once published, the clinical case will be shared on Twitter to encourage discussion among the authors and the broader Twitter audience. Authors are encouraged to actively participate in this engagement process. The written portion of the case report should include a title page and a descriptive text that does not exceed two double-spaced pages, formatted in 12-point Times New Roman font. You may include up to five references and a figure or multimedia legend. Motion clips should be submitted in GIF format, while images should be in JPEG, PNG, or TIFF formats. Other media formats will not be accepted. The title page must include the following details: The full title of the case report. The names of all authors, along with their academic degrees and institutional affiliations. The name and complete mailing address for correspondence, including the street address and post office box. The Twitter account name of the corresponding author. A telephone number and an email address for correspondence.
